candidate.title: ddRADSeq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina DNA-marker-generation schematic for double digest restriction-site associated DNA sequencing (ddRADseq, also called ddRAD). One linear route is shown, ending at amplified DNA. The graph preserves the drawn sequential digests and intervening adapter addition; it is not a literal reconstruction of the Peterson implementation, which uses a simultaneous double digest before ligation. Size selection explains the published reduced representation but is not separately depicted. Other RAD variants and related-publication adaptations are outside this target. The accompanying catalogue mentions optional sample pooling, size selection and combinatorial indexing; these clarify library representation and sample identity but are not extra drawn branches or operations.

states.label: Amplified DNA library
features: Far-right panel is labeled DNA and contains multiple blue lines.
DNA fragments, rather than RNA or probe products, carry the genomic sequence information. Amplification increases copies of adapter-bearing templates.
Published ddRADseq represents a subset of restriction-defined fragments selected by size; the size-selection operation is not drawn here.
The sequenced carrier is the genomic DNA insert in the amplified adapter-bearing library; read sequences can reveal variants in represented loci, while barcode sequence associates reads with samples.
Restriction sites and size selection constrain the sampled loci. This is reduced representation with gaps in genome coverage, not a measurement of every genomic position.
Final blue strokes do not depict adapter removal. Terminal structures are simply not resolved at the final schematic endpoint.

operations.label: Restriction digestion
operations.description: Cut the genomic DNA at restriction sites to produce fragments that subsequently receive barcoded adapters. The initial digest and following adapter addition share a transition into the first fragment panel.
operations.mechanism: Restriction-enzyme cleavage; the drawing gives no enzyme or end chemistry.
operations.information_effect: Restriction-site positions define the first set of fragment boundaries.

operations.label: Second restriction digest
operations.description: As drawn, cut the already barcoded DNA again, producing shorter fragments with retained left barcoded ends and exposed right ends. operations.mechanism: A second restriction cleavage is the depicted transformation. The published simultaneous double digest resolves the intended two-enzyme principle without establishing this drawn temporal order.
operations.information_effect: The second restriction boundary constrains represented genomic fragments instead of a random shearing boundary.

operations.description: Add the second adapter to the exposed opposite ends of the drawn shorter fragments; green right terminal segments appear while first-adapter/barcode ends remain.

operations.label: Amplify
operations.description: Amplify the adapter-bearing fragment templates to obtain the final DNA library shown as multiple blue lines.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and diagram title identify one target, ddRADseq; ddRAD is an alias, not a branch. These operations apply at the declared Illumina schematic scope. The sequential digest/ligation history is retained as drawn and is explicitly distinguished from the cited simultaneous-digest implementation. Mentioned RAD variants, software and plant adaptations are not additional schematic targets. Size selection is needed to interpret which restriction fragments represent the genome, but no local size-selection operation can be positioned from this drawing alone. The colored fragment rows illustrate molecule/barcode diversity; the arrows connect a single workflow, without explicit independently processed branches or a pooling junction.
